standard.title: Participate in guided play-based language activities
standard.description: participate in a range of guided, play-based language activities using formulaic expressions, visual and spoken cues
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and communicate using modelled words and formulaic phrases with support (AC9LSF01). They have limited experience using the target language in structured collaborative activity.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in a range of guided, play-based target language activities — including games, songs, role-plays and collaborative tasks — using formulaic expressions, visual and spoken cues.

nodes.label: Participating in games and songs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in structured language games, songs and chants using formulaic expressions and following spoken and visual cues.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least two different activity types using target language expressions appropriate to each.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in games involving turn-taking, matching, questioning and responding; perform songs and chants with gesture and movement; use spontaneous expressions during play; use digital tools collaboratively for language activities.
wider: Lead a familiar game or song in the target language — calling out instructions or leading a chant for classmates
Use a spontaneous target language expression in an unscripted moment during a game — demonstrating transfer beyond rehearsed contexts
nodes.hinge_reason: Games and songs are the primary interaction context at this band. Students who cannot use formulaic language within structured activities are excluded from the main vehicle for language development, and spontaneous expression in role-play and collaborative tasks is impossible without this base.

response_modes.reason: Formulaic language in games and songs becomes automatic through repeated performance across varied activity types — the game or song is the practice vehicle.

success_criteria: Participates in at least two activity types using appropriate target language expressions
Uses at least one spontaneous expression during a game or activity

nodes.label: Participating in short role-plays
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in short guided role-plays using spoken and visual cues, props and familiar vocabulary to exchange information with a partner.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a short role-play using at least three target language exchanges with a partner.
nodes.typical_width: Take part in role-plays using props and realia across familiar contexts; use question-answer exchange patterns; use actions, gestures and visual supports; exchange information about familiar objects and personal details using modelled language.
wider: Initiate at least one exchange in a role-play without teacher prompting — taking the lead role rather than only responding
Introduce a small improvised element into a role-play — adapting a familiar exchange to a slightly different scenario

response_modes.reason: Role-play participation requires a bank of exchange patterns across varied communicative scenarios before students can apply familiar language to new contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Role-plays are the earliest contexts in which students use the target language for genuine communicative purposes with real exchange stakes. Width investment here builds communicative confidence and positions students as language users.
success_criteria: Participates in a role-play with at least three target language exchanges
Uses at least one question-answer exchange using familiar question forms

nodes.label: Contributing to collaborative class tasks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can contribute to collaborative class tasks and projects using familiar vocabulary — including shared records, displays and class productions.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute at least two target language elements to a collaborative class task.
nodes.typical_width: Contribute to class projects using familiar vocabulary; use digital tools collaboratively for language tasks; exchange, sort and classify items using question-answer patterns; add to shared class resources across the year.
wider: Contribute an original element to a collaborative class project using adapted target language — not only copying modelled text
Use digital tools collaboratively to create a shared target language product — dividing contributions and combining them into a shared output

response_modes.reason: Collaborative task participation develops through varied task types and partner conditions. Students who only contribute to one type of shared task develop narrow collaborative language schemas.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Collaborative tasks produce genuine shared outcomes that belong to the class community — giving target language use a real and lasting audience beyond the individual lesson.
success_criteria: Contributes at least two target language elements to a collaborative class task
Uses familiar vocabulary correctly in at least one shared class resource
